items.cue: One DynamoDB partition key receives most of the traffic
items.detail: A hot key throttles that item collection while the table still has capacity.

items.cue: Aurora reads should scale while writes stay on the writer
items.detail: The reader endpoint load-balances Aurora replicas.

items.cue: The same relational query is the database bottleneck
items.detail: A cache serves repeated reads so the database does less of that work.

items.cue: Users search by words and relevance, not by primary key
items.detail: Search ranking is a different access pattern from a key lookup.

items.cue: The query walks relationships between records
items.detail: A graph store is built for traversals.

items.cue: The application uses a MongoDB-compatible document API
items.detail: DocumentDB is the managed MongoDB-compatible service.

items.cue: The application uses a Cassandra-compatible wide-column API
items.detail: Keyspaces is the managed Cassandra-compatible service.

items.cue: Aurora data written in one Region is read from other Regions
items.detail: Global Database replicates the cluster for cross-Region reads.

items.cue: DynamoDB traffic is spiky and has no steady baseline to buy
items.detail: On-demand bills requests when the rate is not predictable.

items.cue: DynamoDB traffic has a known baseline that should track the load
items.detail: Provisioned capacity fits a baseline, and auto scaling follows the load.

items.cue: An Aurora cluster should change capacity with the load instead of a fixed size
items.detail: Serverless v2 adjusts Aurora capacity as the load changes.

items.cue: A non-production RDS instance is idle between test runs
items.detail: Instance hours stop while it's stopped; storage and backups are still billed, and RDS starts a stopped instance again automatically after a set period.

items.cue: A DynamoDB index is maintained and never queried
items.detail: An index still stores data and receives the writes.

items.cue: Old transactional history stays in the primary database only for an occasional audit
items.answer: Export the cold history to S3
items.detail: The hot store should keep the working set.
items.hook: Audit history can leave the primary.

items.cue: Aurora I/O is the dominant part of a busy cluster's bill
items.detail: I/O-Optimized is the storage choice when I/O charges dominate.

items.cue: Linux instances in more than one Availability Zone mount the same files
items.detail: EFS Standard is a shared file system across Availability Zones.

items.cue: Windows clients need SMB shares with Windows ACLs
items.answer: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server
items.detail: That file system is the managed SMB share.

items.cue: The file system needs multiprotocol access and writable clones
items.detail: ONTAP provides those file-system features.

items.cue: One EC2 volume must sustain high IOPS for a database
items.detail: io2 is the volume type for sustained provisioned IOPS.

items.cue: Volume size, IOPS, and throughput should be chosen separately
items.detail: gp3 sets IOPS and throughput apart from size.

items.cue: A large sequential workload does not need an SSD
items.detail: st1 targets large sequential throughput.

items.cue: The hottest objects are read inside one Availability Zone
items.detail: Express One Zone is the S3 class for that single-AZ hot set.

items.cue: Many clients read different objects from the same bucket at once
items.detail: Prefix spread keeps the request load from stacking on one key range.

items.cue: Object access changes and nobody can name the next class in advance
items.detail: Intelligent-Tiering moves objects by observed access.

items.cue: An archive is rarely retrieved and can wait for a retrieval request
items.detail: Flexible Retrieval is the archive class for that wait.

items.cue: The archive is the coldest data the retention policy keeps
items.detail: Deep Archive is the coldest S3 archive class.

items.cue: Files on the shared Linux file system are rarely opened
items.detail: EFS lifecycle can place rarely read files in Infrequent Access.

items.cue: A recovery-test snapshot is still stored after the test
items.detail: Snapshot storage continues until the snapshot is deleted.
items.hook: The test ended, the snapshot remains.

items.cue: Cross-Region replication is on for a bucket the recovery plan never reads
items.answer: Remove replication the plan does not use
items.detail: Replication stores another copy and issues more requests.
items.hook: No recovery read, no extra copy.

items.cue: Cached public objects are almost never requested from the origin
items.answer: Pair CloudFront with an infrequent S3 class
items.detail: The origin class can be cheaper when the edge serves the repeats.

items.cue: New files in the lake should be classified into the Data Catalog
items.detail: A crawler infers the schema and updates the catalog.

items.cue: A scheduled job should write cleaned objects back to the lake
items.detail: An ETL job is the transform that writes the cleaned data.

items.cue: Catalog access should be granted by database permissions
items.detail: Lake Formation governs access to the lake catalog and its data.

items.cue: A live database must keep replicating to another database during the move
items.detail: DMS replicates the source while it is still changing.

items.cue: The source schema has to be converted for the target engine
items.detail: SCT converts the schema between engines.

items.cue: Partners upload files over SFTP and the objects should land in S3
items.detail: Transfer Family presents the file protocol in front of S3.

items.cue: A SaaS application should send its records to S3 on a schedule
items.detail: AppFlow moves data between SaaS applications and AWS.

items.cue: The network cannot finish the copy in the available time, so the data ships on an appliance
items.detail: Snowball moves the data when the network is the constraint.
items.hook: The network is too slow, ship it.

items.cue: Existing Kafka clients should keep using Kafka APIs
items.detail: MSK is the managed Kafka service.

items.cue: A stream should be transformed as it arrives
items.detail: Flink processes the stream in motion.

items.cue: A large object should upload in parts
items.detail: Multipart upload sends a large object in parallel parts.

items.cue: The same operation must run over a large set of objects that are already in the bucket
items.detail: Batch Operations applies one job across existing objects.

items.cue: On-premises clients should keep using NFS or SMB while the bytes are stored as objects
items.detail: File Gateway presents the file share and stores objects in S3.

items.cue: A data set in S3 should be processed through a high-throughput file system and written back
items.answer: Amazon FSx for Lustre linked to S3
items.detail: Lustre can use S3 as its linked data repository.

items.cue: A volume's contents have to move by copying its point-in-time image
items.detail: A snapshot copy carries the volume data to the destination.
items.hook: Move the volume by its snapshot.

items.cue: Callers need an HTTP API in front of private functions
items.detail: API Gateway is the HTTP front for the functions.
items.hook: HTTP in front of the function.

items.cue: A multi-step workflow needs its own retries and state between services
items.detail: Step Functions keeps the workflow state between steps.

items.cue: A source should feed a target with filtering, without a custom poller
items.detail: Pipes connects a source to a target with optional filtering.

items.cue: A queue should invoke the function when messages arrive
items.detail: The mapping polls the queue and invokes the function.

items.cue: After an asynchronous function finishes, the result should go to a queue or another function
items.detail: Destinations route the success or failure result.

items.cue: Clients should ask for the fields they need over GraphQL
items.detail: AppSync is the managed GraphQL service.

items.cue: Work runs on a schedule and no server should stay up to wait for it
items.detail: Scheduler starts the target on the schedule.

items.cue: The HTTP caller should be accepted quickly while the job finishes later
items.answer: Queue between the API and the worker
items.detail: The queue lets the API return before the worker finishes.

items.cue: A latency-sensitive function must avoid cold starts
items.detail: Provisioned concurrency keeps execution environments ready.
items.hook: Ready environments for the sensitive function.

items.cue: One function must not be able to consume the account's concurrency
items.detail: Reserved concurrency caps that function.

items.cue: An instance needs a higher packet rate than a standard network interface
items.detail: Enhanced networking uses the Elastic Network Adapter.

items.cue: HPC instances in one Availability Zone need to be placed close together
items.detail: A cluster placement group packs those instances together.

items.cue: Capacity should be added in defined steps as a metric crosses bands
items.detail: Step scaling adds capacity by those bands.

items.cue: An ECS service should draw capacity from a named provider
items.detail: A capacity provider supplies the cluster capacity the service uses.
items.hook: The service draws from a provider.

items.cue: The working set does not fit in a general-purpose instance
items.detail: That family is the choice when memory is the bottleneck.

items.cue: Every account's API history should land in a separate log-archive account
items.detail: An organization trail records member accounts into the archive account.

items.cue: Someone needs to know which resources are shared outside the zone of trust
items.detail: Access Analyzer reports access from outside that zone.

items.cue: Workforce access should be a permission set, not a long-lived IAM user key
items.detail: A permission set is the assignment Identity Center gives the workforce.

items.cue: An S3 action should succeed only when it arrives through one VPC endpoint
items.answer: IAM condition on the VPC endpoint
items.detail: The condition key ties the API call to that endpoint.

items.cue: A human role should be unusable until MFA is present
items.answer: Require MFA on the human role
items.detail: The role policy can require MFA.

items.cue: Trail files should be checkable for tampering after delivery
items.detail: Validation detects a changed, added, or deleted log file.

items.cue: An administrator wants the services an identity has actually used
items.detail: Access Advisor shows the last use of allowed services.

items.cue: A temporary session should be narrower than the role it assumes
items.answer: Session policy on the assumed role
items.detail: A session policy can only reduce the role's permissions.
items.hook: The session is narrower than the role.

items.cue: Traffic inside the VPC needs stateful inspection before it reaches the workload
items.detail: Network Firewall inspects traffic in the VPC.

items.cue: Operators need a shell on an instance and no inbound port should be open
items.answer: Session Manager with no inbound port
items.detail: Session Manager reaches the instance through Systems Manager, so the security group does not need an inbound management port.

items.cue: Threat detection should come from the account's logs
items.detail: GuardDuty analyzes those logs for threats.

items.cue: A public bucket or an open administrative rule should be detected as configuration drift
items.detail: Config evaluates the resource against the rule.

items.cue: Findings from several security services should be in one place
items.detail: Security Hub aggregates those findings.

items.cue: Workloads and images should be scanned for software vulnerabilities
items.detail: Inspector scans the workloads and images.

items.cue: Instances that only receive load-balancer traffic should have no internet-gateway route
items.answer: Private subnet behind the load balancer
items.detail: A private subnet has no direct route to the internet gateway.
items.hook: No internet route for those instances.

items.cue: The bucket key must be one the key policy can deny even when the bucket allows the read
items.answer: SSE-KMS with a customer managed key
items.detail: The customer managed key adds a key policy to the read path.
items.hook: The key policy can still deny the read.

items.cue: Many objects should share KMS work instead of calling KMS for every object
items.detail: A bucket key reduces the KMS requests for SSE-KMS objects.

items.cue: New objects should be encrypted even when the upload request names no key
items.detail: Default encryption applies when the upload does not specify one.
items.hook: No key on the request, still encrypted.

items.cue: New EBS volumes in the Region should be encrypted without a per-volume setting
items.detail: The Region setting encrypts new volumes.

items.cue: An existing unencrypted RDS database has to become encrypted
items.answer: Copy a snapshot to an encrypted snapshot
items.detail: RDS encryption is applied by restoring from an encrypted snapshot copy.

items.cue: A database password must rotate on a schedule and stay out of the task definition
items.detail: Rotation stores and replaces the secret on the schedule.

items.cue: Access to a KMS key is decided first by the key's own policy
items.detail: The key policy is the root control on that key.
items.hook: The key's own policy comes first.

items.cue: Another principal needs temporary, limited use of a key
items.detail: A grant delegates a specific use of the key.

items.cue: The data is encrypted with a data key, and KMS encrypts that data key
items.detail: Envelope encryption keeps the data key under KMS.

items.cue: The same ciphertext must be decrypted in another Region
items.detail: A multi-Region key has related keys that decrypt that ciphertext in the other Region.

items.cue: An object must stay for the retention period, and nobody can shorten it
items.detail: Compliance mode blocks shortening or deleting the object through the retention period.

items.cue: Deleting an object version should require a second factor
items.detail: MFA Delete requires MFA for that versioned delete.
items.hook: A second factor to delete the version.

items.cue: AWS should store ciphertext and never see the plaintext
items.detail: The client encrypts the data before the upload.

items.cue: A DynamoDB table should use a key the account controls
items.detail: DynamoDB encryption at rest can use that key.
items.hook: The account's key on the table.

items.cue: Object requests that are not on TLS should be rejected
items.detail: The bucket policy denies the request when the transport is not secure.

items.cue: HTTP host and path rules choose the target group
items.detail: An ALB routes HTTP by those rules.
items.hook: Host and path pick the target.

items.cue: A TCP service needs a static address and the client source IP
items.detail: An NLB serves TCP with a static address and can preserve the source IP.

items.cue: Traffic should pass through a firewall appliance fleet
items.detail: A Gateway Load Balancer inserts that appliance fleet in the path.
items.hook: The appliance fleet sits in the path.

items.cue: Two VPCs need private routes and there is no hub yet
items.detail: Peering connects two VPCs directly.

items.cue: The DNS answer should follow the user's location rather than measured latency
items.detail: Geolocation routing uses the user's location.

items.cue: Viewers must not be able to bypass CloudFront and read the bucket directly
items.detail: Origin Access Control limits the bucket to CloudFront.

items.cue: Each Availability Zone should egress without depending on another zone's NAT
items.answer: NAT gateway in each Availability Zone
items.detail: A NAT gateway in the zone keeps that egress local to the zone.
items.hook: Each zone has its own NAT.

items.cue: A private link to the office is needed and a dedicated circuit is not justified
items.detail: Site-to-Site VPN builds that link over the internet.

items.cue: Heavy application-to-database traffic is crossing Availability Zones
items.detail: Same-AZ placement avoids the cross-AZ data charge on that flow.
items.hook: Keep the heavy flow in one zone.

items.cue: Every spoke VPC has its own interface endpoint for the same service
items.answer: Share one endpoint from a central VPC
items.detail: One shared endpoint replaces an hourly endpoint in every spoke.

items.cue: A function needs no resources inside a VPC
items.answer: Leave the function outside a VPC
items.detail: A function outside a VPC reaches the internet without a NAT gateway.

items.cue: Users are in one Region and a global accelerator adds an hourly charge
items.answer: Skip Global Accelerator for a single-Region audience
items.detail: A regional load balancer already serves that audience.

items.cue: A steady high volume to the data center justifies a private circuit
items.answer: AWS Direct Connect for a steady private circuit
items.detail: Direct Connect is the private circuit for that steady volume.

items.cue: Each object is downloaded once, so an edge cache would not be reused
items.answer: Skip the CDN for one-time downloads
items.detail: A CDN pays off when the same object is requested again.

items.cue: Distant clients upload large objects slowly, and clients near the Region do not
items.answer: S3 Transfer Acceleration for the distant uploads
items.detail: Transfer Acceleration uses the edge network when distance is the constraint. Clients near the Region can use a standard upload.

items.cue: A target should leave rotation when its application path fails
items.answer: Health check on the application path
items.detail: The load balancer uses that check to stop sending traffic.
items.hook: The path fails, the target leaves.

items.cue: An unhealthy EC2 instance should be replaced
items.detail: The group replaces an instance that fails its health check.

items.cue: The compute group itself should exist in more than one Availability Zone
items.answer: Auto Scaling group spanning Availability Zones
items.detail: The group launches across the zones it is given.
items.hook: The group covers more than one zone.

items.cue: Aurora storage should survive loss of one Availability Zone
items.detail: Aurora replicates the volume across Availability Zones.

items.cue: A load balancer should send traffic to healthy targets in every enabled Availability Zone
items.detail: Cross-zone load balancing can send a request to a healthy target in another zone.
items.hook: A healthy target in any enabled zone.

items.cue: DynamoDB writes in several Regions must all be active
items.detail: Global tables replicate the table for multi-Region writes.

items.cue: Shared Linux files must remain available after one Availability Zone is lost
items.detail: EFS Standard stores the file system across Availability Zones.

items.cue: Frequently read objects must survive loss of one Availability Zone
items.detail: S3 Standard stores those objects across Availability Zones.
items.hook: Frequent objects, more than one zone.

items.cue: Objects must also exist in a second Region
items.detail: Replication copies the objects to the other Region.
items.hook: A copy in the second Region.

items.cue: A Regional database failure should promote a secondary that was already receiving the writes
items.detail: The secondary cluster can be promoted.
items.hook: Promote the secondary that already has the writes.

items.cue: The caller waits on the request until the function returns
items.detail: The caller receives the function result on that request.

items.cue: The caller should not wait, and retries happen after the response
items.detail: Asynchronous invocation returns before the retries finish.

items.cue: A failing dependency should be retried with increasing delay
items.detail: Backoff keeps the retries from stampeding the dependency.

items.cue: A setting change should not require a new machine image
items.detail: Parameter Store holds the setting outside the image.
items.hook: The setting lives outside the image.

items.cue: Clients need a stable name while instances are replaced
items.detail: Clients use the load balancer name, and the instances behind it can change.
items.hook: Clients use the load balancer name.
